newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee closes retraces to lower close.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee closes retraces to lower close.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures pulled back slightly on Thursday, one day after climbing to their highest level in two years, as speculators took profits on the market's sweeping rally, trading sources said.
Prices shot higher at the opening on momentum from yesterday's 10-cent rise, but the buying interest faded before the market could test new life-of-contract highs set Wednesday.
The market then retreated below unchanged, where it held for the remainder of the session. Scale-down buying on the part of U.S. roasters helped stem the losses, traders said.

"It's just a little bit of profit-taking, it's nothing to get too excited about," said one broker. "The market still looks very constructive."Scale-down buying from the roasting sector offered support at the lows, they said.

Benchmark May futures fell 1.75 cent per lb, to close at 171.10 cents, toward the bottom of today's 169-175.60 range. Spot March delivery ended down 2.35 cents, at 183.10, after touching a contract high of 192 cents early on.

After watching the market swing wildly on Wednesday before closing near the day's highs, traders said many dealers opted to remain on the sidelines today. Volume on the exchange totaled 8,856 lots, compared with yesterday's unusually hefty tally of 15,742.
"People got beat up yesterday, and they didn't want the same thing to happen today," a second trader said.

Options volume remained fairly steady, however, as traders bought out-of-the-money puts as a hedge against a sudden downturn. April puts were well bid at the 145, 150 and 160-cent strikes, traders said.
On the charts, May futures would encounter light resistance at 172.50, followed by 177 cents. Support was noted in the 165.60-166 range.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
